The `real-run/` directory itself isn't in the diff at all — `git log`/`git status` in the worktree show it untracked (only `mock-run/` and `task.jsonl`'s log lines about it were committed, in `3523f5ec`/`5a8eca96`). If this branch merges as reviewed, the one piece of real-run evidence that does exist never lands with it.

`Server/collab.mjs:117-122` (`mockFacts`'s comment) says the merged mock has one settled fact because "every member but one calls it settled — still settled, since deliverable 2's rule is 'every member who LISTED it'" — that's backwards: the merge rule requires *every* lister to say settled, so the fact where only one of three members (sonnet-b) says settled actually merges to `likely` (confirmed in `mock-run/collab.jsonl`: `"a-member-never-votes-for-itself"` → `"certainty":"likely"`). The fact that actually stays settled is the *other* one, where all three agree. The code's behavior is correct; only the comment misdescribes which fact ends up which certainty and why — worth a fix so a future reader doesn't trust the wrong rule.

`checkDisputes` (`Server/collab.mjs`, `disputeFileFor`/`JSON.parse` block) only deletes `dispute.json` after a successful parse; if a member writes a syntactically invalid `dispute.json`, the `catch { continue; }` skips the `unlinkSync` too, so that same broken file gets re-read (and re-fail) every subsequent phase for the rest of the run. Harmless (no crash, no duplicate log line) but it never self-heals — a stray line noting "delete it either way" would close this off.
